The same commit fixed a disposition-table conflation and a template field assuming output a refutation never produces. 0e119a109 added a converse-guard test proving every plugin root shipping reviewer-findings on disk is covered by the hand-maintained PLUGIN_ROOTS map, via the canonical check_plugin_frontmatter_self_containment.plugin_roots() helper rather than a raw filesystem walk.

While 59ba674c5/0e119a109 were staged locally (not yet pushed), Cursor Bugbot's Autofix cloud agent pushed 35f56343b directly to this branch: a colliding push from an external automated agent, not a human or this session. It rewrote the same git grep -f fix to git grep -n -F -e "$NEEDLE" and added a second, competing converse-guard test to conftest.py using a raw REPO_ROOT.rglob("skills/reviewer-findings/SKILL.md") walk. Investigated both before reconciling: re-ran the same subprocess reproduction against -e "$NEEDLE" and it still false-confirmed on the needle's second line alone, so -e carries the identical defect as -f; the raw rglob walk descends into the nested checkouts under .claude/worktrees/ that .claude/rules/plugin-self-containment.md documents as a known trap (independently flagged by a fresh Copilot review on the same PR), and it referenced REPO_ROOT, a name that exists only in _helpers.py, so the auto-merged conftest.py would have raised NameError at collection. A ninth Copilot review round (4 comments) on PR #5178 found the eighth round's own fix was lossy: NEEDLE=$(cat <needle-file>) and PATH_SPEC=$(cat <path-file>) both use plain command substitution, which strips every trailing newline the file has, so a needle ending in blank lines is searched as a shorter string than the finding quoted, and a cited path ending in a newline is silently truncated to a different, possibly pre-existing path (CWE-20). Verified empirically: X=$(cat f) on a file ending in two newlines loses both; X=$(cat f; printf x); X=${X%x} (append a sentinel byte, strip it back off) round-trips the bytes exactly. Fixed by requiring the sentinel idiom at all 4 call sites across reviewer-findings/SKILL.md (3) and pr-comment-responder/references/workflow.md (1). While investigating, found the QA report's existing claim that the redundant [ -s <needle-file> ] check had been dropped in round five did not match the shipped SKILL.md (still present in 3 places, reintroduced accidentally during the round-six CWE-78 rewrite); fixed by removing it, making the report's claim true rather than rewriting the report to describe the wrong reality. New test file tests/skills/reviewer-findings/test_reviewer_findings_trailing_newline_safety.py (kept separate from the 449-line test_reviewer_findings_premise_verification.py to stay under the 500-line taste-count-ratchet ceiling): positive coverage for the needle and path recipes across both plugin roots plus workflow.md, and a negative control proving the check requires the exact sentinel recipe, not any "$(cat" substring (the fix's own warning prose names the bad pattern too).
